The surrender 'ceded Diriyah and nearby cities to the Ottomans in exchange for the Saudis' safety'; Muhammad Ali then ordered the city razed; Abdullah was beheaded in Istanbul. History of Saudi Arabia: the Egyptians 'destroyed the power of the Al Saud' in 1818, held the Hejaz until 1840, and the Al Saud returned in 1824. [fx-36 H20, 1 Nov 2026: region narrowed from Cliopatria's whole 1815 shape (3,727 cells) to the part of it in the Hejaz and Najd without Ha'il (1,346 cells). Wahhabi War page: 'By 1817, the armies had overrun Rass, Buraida and Unayza', 'In December 1819, Ibrahim Pasha returned to Egypt after formally incorporating Hejaz into the Ottoman Empire' and 'Central Arabia became a region of permanent Wahhabi uprisings'; Emirate of Diriyah page: Ibrahim Pasha 'led Ottoman forces into the heart of Najd, capturing town after town'. The pages never give the Egyptians the Northern Borders (469 cells), Al-Jawf (332), Ha'il (452), the Gulf coast (Ash Sharqiyah 692, Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait) or the Iraqi and Jordanian fringe; these were 1,350 of the cells that muhammad-ali-dynasty's 1840 snap removed. Ha'il is left out as in muhammad-ali-dynasty /ledger/17 (the Rashidi emirate).]

notes: Page budget (9 pages) spent. Nothing opened dates the growth of 1762-1783, the Qasim and Sudair additions of 1769-1788, the reach to Asir, Najran and the Tihama (1794-1803), or the eastern reach to Bandar Abbas and the Syrian desert edge: those shapes are ok or unverified and the three Asir and Tihama gains are confidence 1 at Cliopatria's years. Disagreements: Mecca 1803 (Emirate, Abdulaziz, Wahhabi War) vs 1806 (Saud, History of Saudi Arabia); Karbala 1801 (Emirate) vs 1802; Al-Hasa 1789 / 1792 (Saud page) vs 1795 (Abdulaziz page); Taif 1802 (Abdulaziz) vs 1803 (Emirate); first Saudi State from 1727 (History of Saudi Arabia) vs 1744. The Emirate page has no infobox area, so no area comparison was possible. Cliopatria rows: shape 1744 omits the Diriyah cell; Riyadh is outside until 1788 though captured 1773; Al-Ahsa stays partial 1791-1802; Buraimi is inside from 1800 but taken 1805; Medina, Mecca and Jeddah stay in the 1812 shape after their fall; the 1815 shape runs to 1819 and keeps Al-Qassim after 1817. The shape's end 1819 vs the state's 9 September 1818. Counterparts needing dossiers: the Bani Khalid Emirate (Al-Hasa to 1795), Dahham ibn Dawwas's Riyadh (to 1773), the Sharifate of Mecca (Ghalib; Hejaz under the Ottomans), Asir and Najran tribes. Gazetteer names missing: place 'Diriyah' (24.734 N, 46.575 E; used as lon/lat radius), place 'Khurma' (Hejaz, near Taif). Bahrain: a vassal tint with the House of Khalifa 1802-1818; the end is a bridging judgement. Natural Earth spelling used: admin1 'Al Quassim', 'Al Buraymi', place 'Al Ayn', 'Yanbu al Bahr', 'At Taif'. Karbala and Najaf raids are in wars with empty zones (no ground held).
